UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Cause: Rotten food, burned food, or stale food.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, endurance drain, increased hunger and thirst.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Prevention: Eat fresh food and avoid food that has spoiled, burned badly, or gone stale.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Treatment: Anti-nausea tablets, electrolyte powder, and activated charcoal. Activated charcoal can cure it over time.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Cause: Eating with bloody or dirty hands.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Symptoms: Severe nausea, vomiting, dehydration, stomach pain, and fatigue.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Prevention: Wash hands before eating. Soap and clean water are best.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Treatment: Anti-diarrheal medicine, electrolyte powder, antiviral capsules, or IV ciprofloxacin for severe bacterial cases.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Cause: Raw or undercooked wild game and unsafe raw meat.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Symptoms: Intense muscle pain, fever, weakness, and dangerous health loss in severe stages.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Prevention: Cook meat thoroughly, especially wild game.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Treatment: Muscle relaxants and anti-inflammatory medicine for symptoms; antiparasitic pills or albendazole injection to cure.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Cause: Poisonous berries, poisonous mushrooms, or other toxic food.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Symptoms: Violent nausea, vomiting, dizziness, blurred vision, weakness, and dangerous systemic poisoning.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Prevention: Avoid unidentified wild food unless you can verify it is safe.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Treatment: Activated charcoal is the main treatment. Anti-nausea tablets and electrolytes help symptoms.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Cause: Tainted water or severe gastrointestinal contamination.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Symptoms: Severe diarrhea, vomiting, dehydration, fever, weakness, and possible blood loss.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Prevention: Drink clean or boiled water and avoid unsafe water sources.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Treatment: Electrolytes and anti-diarrheal medicine for symptoms; IV ciprofloxacin for severe bacterial infection.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Cause: Cold, wet, or prolonged exposure while exhausted.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Symptoms: Coughing, sneezing, mild fever, fatigue, and reduced stamina.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Prevention: Stay warm, dry, rested, and protected from bad weather.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Treatment: Rest, fluids, cough medicine, antipyretics for fever; Cold & Flu tablets or antiviral capsules can cure it over time.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Cause: Severe or untreated respiratory illness, cold exposure, or weakened health.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Symptoms: Fever, coughing, chest pain, endurance loss, and potentially lethal respiratory failure.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Prevention: Treat respiratory illness early and avoid prolonged cold exposure.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Treatment: Prescription or broad spectrum antibiotics cure over time; IV Ciprofloxacin is the fast clinical cure. Bronchodilator helps breathing, cough medicine suppresses coughing, antipyretics reduce fever.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Cause: Low body temperature from cold, wet clothing, wind, or exposure.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Symptoms: Shivering, weakness, confusion, fatigue, and dangerous temperature drop.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Prevention: Wear insulation, stay dry, and get indoors during severe cold.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Treatment: Warm up, change into dry clothes, rest, and use external heat sources.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Cause: Heat exposure, dehydration, heavy clothing, or exertion in hot weather.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Symptoms: Dizziness, nausea, weakness, thirst, fatigue, and overheating.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Prevention: Hydrate, rest in shade, wear lighter clothing, and avoid overexertion in heat.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Treatment: Cool down, rest, drink water, and use electrolyte powder.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Incubation: Can develop from untreated heat exhaustion.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Duration: Critical until body temperature is controlled.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Cause: Extreme heat exposure or severe dehydration.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Symptoms: Extreme body temperature, delirium, confusion, vomiting, collapse/blackouts, dehydration, and life-threatening health loss.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Prevention: Avoid extreme heat, hydrate aggressively, and treat heat exhaustion early.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Treatment: Immediate cooling. Instant ice packs can cure heat stroke with a 4-dose cooling course; fluids and electrolytes help dehydration.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Cause: Prolonged exposure to decomposing corpses, especially in enclosed spaces.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Symptoms: Eye irritation, nausea, dizziness, weakness, coughing, and possible collapse at high exposure.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Prevention: Ventilate corpse-filled spaces and wear effective face protection.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Treatment: Fresh air immediately. Anti-nausea tablets help symptoms; respiratory support kit or corticosteroids can treat severe cases.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Cau: Fungal spores from decomposing corpses in damp, wet, or cold conditions.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Sym: Respiratory irritation, fever, coughing, wheezing, endurance loss, and weakness.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Pre: Wear face protection near damp corpse-filled areas and avoid breathing contaminated air.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Tre: Bronchodilator inhaler and antipyretics for symptoms; antifungal tablets or IV amphotericin to cure.
UI_EHR_Codex_tuberculosis_Cause: Long-term respiratory exposure in contaminated corpse-heavy environments.
UI_EHR_Codex_tuberculosis_Symptoms: Persistent cough, fever, fatigue, weight loss, night sweats, and coughing blood in severe cases.
UI_EHR_Codex_tuberculosis_Prevention: Avoid prolonged corpse exposure and wear respiratory protection.
UI_EHR_Codex_tuberculosis_Treatment: TB antibiotics or rifampicin combo pack. Cough suppressants and antipyretics only reduce symptoms.
UI_EHR_Codex_wound_infection_Cause: Dirty wounds, poor bandaging, or untreated injury contamination.
UI_EHR_Codex_wound_infection_Symptoms: Pain, swelling, redness, pus, fever, and worsening wound condition.
UI_EHR_Codex_wound_infection_Prevention: Clean wounds, use sterile bandages, and change dirty bandages quickly.
UI_EHR_Codex_wound_infection_Treatment: Disinfect wounds, use antibiotic ointment, and escalate to antibiotics if infection spreads.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Cause: A spreading bacterial skin infection after a poorly closed wound. Rough suturing has a high risk of starting cellulitis.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Symptoms: Hot red skin, swelling, local pain, fever, fatigue, weakness, and reduced endurance. Untreated stage 4 can progress into sepsis.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Prevention: Clean wounds before suturing, use sterile supplies, and avoid rough stitching when possible.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Treatment: Antibiotic ointment can treat mild cases. Prescription antibiotics, broad-spectrum antibiotics, plant-based antibiotics, IV antibiotics, or IV vancomycin treat more serious cases. Anti-inflammatory and antipyretic tablets reduce symptoms only.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Cause: Untreated severe infection entering the bloodstream.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Symptoms: High fever, extreme weakness, confusion, rapid decline, and life-threatening systemic illness.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Prevention: Treat wound infections and cellulitis before they spread.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Treatment: IV antibiotics and aggressive medical support. This is an emergency condition.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Cause: Deep contaminated puncture wounds, rusty metal injuries, or severe dirty wounds.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Symptoms: Jaw stiffness, muscle spasms, pain, fever, and dangerous neuromuscular failure.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Prevention: Clean deep wounds quickly and use tetanus prophylaxis when possible.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Treatment: Muscle relaxants for symptoms; tetanus antitoxin or tetanus immunoglobulin with a syringe to cure.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Caus: Prolonged exposure to contaminated dirt or grass. The first bite leaves a scratch-like wound.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Symp: Severe itching, repeated scratch wounds, bite-site pain, fever, and dangerous health decline in late stages.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Prev: Avoid lingering on bare dirt or grass when possible, cover exposed skin, and keep wounds clean.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Trea: Topical permethrin is the main treatment. Antiparasitic pills can also cure it, but the course is longer.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Cause: A hard head impact from a height fall or serious vehicle crash.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Symptoms: Headache, dizziness, blurred vision, nausea, and disorientation that gradually improves over time.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Prevention: Avoid high falls and severe crashes. Treat head impacts as dangerous even if you can still walk.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Treatment: No direct cure. Rest and time are the main treatment; symptom medicine can make recovery easier.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Cause: Extreme stress held at its breaking point for many hours.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Symptoms: Hallucinated sounds, irrational speech, visual distortion, and unsafe impulsive behavior.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Prevention: Reduce stress before it reaches a prolonged maximum state.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Treatment: Antipsychotics. Requires an 8-dose course over 4 days.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Duration: 2-4 days without treatment; can become fatal quickly.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Cause: Receiving blood that is incompatible with your body.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Symptoms: Lower back pain, severe weakness, nausea, high fever, hemolysis, endurance loss, and dangerous health decline.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Prevention: Use compatible blood and test compatibility whenever possible.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Treatment: IV fluids and furosemide are the main treatments. Antipyretics, anti-nausea tablets, and anti-inflammatory pills reduce symptoms.
UI_EHR_Codex_knox_infection_Symptoms: Fever, nausea, weakness, pale skin, and terminal systemic infection.
